args.summary:
I played a new game as Akkad from the start screen up to turn 11. Things that worked: world setup, the map and its gold/research numbers, event cards, autosave on every turn, and the city build list. Where I got stuck:
1. Diplomacy: Demand tribute did nothing on the first tap. The second tap said it needs a decree, but the card never mentions decrees.
2. War: declaring war costs 300 gold, which I couldn't afford by turn 10.
3. Naval: Kish's Units list has no ship at all, not even a locked one saying which tech it needs.
4. Help: the How to play tutorial is 3 short pages and says nothing about battles, ships or decrees.
5. Speed: a warband takes 19 turns, which is very slow.
I never got a battle, a ship, the glossary index or the World Congress in this session, so those checks are still open for the next one. The early game is calm but feels thin for someone new.

thought: Out of steps. I liked the start but got stuck on boats and fights.

args.summary: Covered every checklist area. Highlights: the siege battles look great, the tips are helpful, and the Enemy button with Attack it works well. The battle result screen hides its Continue button below the fold. In the first siege I won but lost more men than the enemy, which felt bad, and the loot line was confusing. Pontus attacked Jerusalem again right away, two turns later, and this time Auto gives me only 13%. Repeat sieges come fast and could wear players down. The pre-battle odds panel is clear. Turn flow, the era goal pick and the advisor's build suggestions are easy for a new player. Overall fun, and pacing is mostly good.

args.summary: I played on from turn 116 to turn 126 as Israel while at war with Akkad. Things that worked well: event cards, the ruler points screen, seating governors, founding Gezer and the turn report with its Defend and Engage buttons. Problems I hit: 1) I couldn't find a city by name. The button I hoped was search opened zoom controls instead. 2) In march mode, tapping a city picked the wrong one (Damascus, not Shechem) and the map jumped. 3) When I fought the Siege of Shechem on Auto, it showed no result screen. The window also said Auto would hold 100% with 1,500 militia against 20,000 attackers, which seems wrong. On turn 126 Shechem still looks like mine and asks for a build, but I only found that out by checking the map. Overall pacing feels good and the to-do list on the left keeps me busy. Fun 4.

thought: Shechem seems to have held. I'm wrapping up the session here.
